method: split-ln2 range reduction; degree-6 Taylor polynomial; memcpy binary32 power-of-two scaling
dense_sampling: 2,000,001 uniformly spaced real locations cast to float32 over [-80,0]
boundary_sampling: 115 nearest-log2 boundaries, center plus four adjacent float32 inputs on both sides
fallback_policy: For x outside [-80,0], including NaN and infinities, return expf(x). Non-binary32 implementations also return expf(x).
scope: Short numerical characterization only; no training benchmark or learned-quality evaluation.
limitations: Dense and edge sampling is not an exhaustive proof for every float32 input.
Taylor remainder bound covers real-arithmetic polynomial truncation, excluding range-reduction and floating-point rounding.
Fast-domain errno and floating-point exception flags are not promised to match libm.
Performance and full-step numerical checks are evaluated separately by the shared experiment runner.
